standard.title: Statistical investigations
standard.description: Conduct statistical investigations, collecting data through survey responses and other methods; record and display data using digital tools; interpret the data and communicate the results
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can conduct guided statistical investigations involving collection, representation and interpretation of data (AC9M3ST03). They have not yet independently designed survey instruments or accessed data from online sources.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan and conduct statistical investigations, using surveys and other data sources, displaying and interpreting results using digital tools.

nodes.label: Pose and plan
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can pose a statistical question and plan how to collect relevant data.
nodes.minimum_width: Pose one statistical question and identify what data needs to be collected to answer it; describe how the data will be collected.
nodes.typical_width: Pose and refine statistical questions for different contexts; identify the most appropriate data collection method (survey, observation, secondary data); create survey questions that will produce useful data; plan the investigation before collecting.
wider: Investigate a consumer context (e.g. product placement in supermarkets) by identifying exactly what questions need to be answered and what data is needed — distinguishing relevant from irrelevant information
Compare what different types of data sources (own survey vs secondary data) can and cannot tell you about the same question

response_modes.reason: Students often jump to data collection without asking whether the planned data can actually answer their question. The planning scaffold — 'what question am I asking? what data answers it? how will I collect that data?' — is the key reasoning move that separates purposeful investigation from accidental data gathering.

nodes.hinge_reason: Students who collect data without verifying it can answer their question arrive at Node 3 with data that cannot support a meaningful interpretation. The investigation cycle breaks at the communication phase when the collected data and the original question are misaligned.
success_criteria: Students can pose a clear statistical question and identify what data is needed to answer it
Students can create a survey question that will produce data relevant to their question

nodes.label: Collect and record
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can collect data using surveys or digital sources and record it systematically using digital tools.
nodes.minimum_width: Collect data using one method (survey or online source); record the data in a digital table or spreadsheet.
nodes.typical_width: Collect data through surveys, observation and digital sources; record using digital tables, tally sheets or spreadsheets; access online databases or query interfaces where appropriate; organise data for analysis.
wider: Access and retrieve data from an online query interface (weather records, Google Trends) to investigate a question that cannot be answered by a class survey
Compare data from a class survey with secondary data from an online source about the same question, noting similarities and differences
success_criteria: Students can collect and record data systematically using a digital tool
Students can identify whether their data is fit-for-purpose for answering the original question

nodes.label: Interpret and communicate
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interpret data from their investigation and communicate findings in terms of the original question.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one finding from a data display and communicate it in a sentence that references the original question.
nodes.typical_width: Interpret data displays and describe the main findings; communicate results in terms of the original question to a relevant audience; discuss whether the data supports or challenges initial predictions; identify at least one limitation of the investigation.
wider: Compare investigation findings with predictions made before data collection, discussing what was surprising and how the evidence relates to initial assumptions
Present statistical findings to a real audience (class, another grade, principal) using appropriate language and visual displays, adapting communication to the audience's background

response_modes.reason: A statistical investigation is an integrated cycle — posing, collecting, displaying, and interpreting must all align for the communication to be coherent. The integration failure mode is a report that describes the display without connecting back to the original question. Communicating results demands students coordinate all phases.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Statistical investigations with real audiences and genuine questions are authentically engaging and develop transferable inquiry skills. The iterative comparison with prior predictions builds scientific thinking habits.
success_criteria: Students can state at least one finding from their investigation in terms of the original question
Students can communicate results to an audience using appropriate language and a clear data display
